rows.title: PluginVersion record and field offsets
rows.titleFr: Record `PluginVersion` et offsets

preconditions: x64 process; the SDK is x64-only.
scenario.operation: Compare the managed PluginVersion record with the header-derived x64 layout and call GetVersion through the host record.
scenario.expected: Size 16 bytes, Version at offset 0 and PluginName at offset 8 with the padding untouched; GetVersion writes version 6 and the bootstrap name pointer.

rows.title: Compact bootstrap record between guard bytes
rows.titleFr: Record bootstrap compact avec sentinelles autour

preconditions: The host hands a 36-byte buffer for the packed PluginInitRecord.
scenario.operation: Run the managed bootstrap on a buffer surrounded by guard bytes, at an aligned and at an odd address (C3: tail canary read around the host buffer).
scenario.expected: Exactly the 36 record bytes change; every guard byte keeps its value.

rows.title: Reduced managed exports table or missing pointer
rows.titleFr: Table managée réduite ou pointeur manquant

preconditions: The bootstrap has run.
scenario.operation: Enable with a null exports record, an undersized record or a record without GetLuaState (C3: record the exports size the host reports).
scenario.expected: The enable is refused and logged before any read past the reported size and before any Lua or plugin call.

rows.title: Observation of the second bootstrap integer
rows.titleFr: Observation du deuxième entier du bootstrap

preconditions: LiveProbe built from the exact CI package and loaded on the qualifiable profile.
scenario.operation: Read the raw second CEPluginInitialize argument from ce77_live_probe_status_json().
scenario.expected: The raw integer is recorded as observed, with no size, length or version meaning attached.

rows.title: Name before enable, then enable, disable and enable
rows.titleFr: Nom avant enable, puis enable/disable/enable

preconditions: LiveProbe built from the exact CI package and loaded on the qualifiable profile.
scenario.operation: Read the plugin name before the first enable, then enable, disable and enable again, recording plugin id and epoch each time.
scenario.expected: The name is stable, one plugin instance is reused and every enable gets a new epoch.

rows.title: Non-ASCII plugin name
rows.titleFr: nom non ASCII

preconditions: LiveProbe built with -p:LiveProbeNonAsciiName=true.
scenario.operation: Load the non-ASCII variant and record the name bytes the SDK wrote and the name Cheat Engine shows (operator observation).
scenario.expected: The decoding Cheat Engine applies (ANSI code page or UTF-8) is recorded; the name never corrupts the record or the plugin list.

rows.title: Exception during construction or enable
rows.titleFr: Exception pendant construction / enable

preconditions: LiveProbe loaded; C3 uses liveprobe.fault.json with throwIn FactoryCreate or OnEnable.
scenario.operation: Make the plugin constructor or OnEnable throw.
scenario.expected: Cheat Engine is told the enable failed, no exception crosses an ABI callback, the runtime is detached, the failure is logged and a later enable can succeed.

rows.title: Re-entrant disable from a running callback
rows.titleFr: Disable réentrant depuis callback en cours

preconditions: The plugin is enabled; C3 runs ce77_live_probe_pump_messages while the operator unticks the plugin.
scenario.operation: Request a disable while a lifecycle transition, an admitted Lua operation or dispatched main-thread work of the same plugin is still running.
scenario.expected: The nested disable is refused with a defined result and a log entry, without waiting on itself; the outer transition stands.

rows.title: Partial cleanup, then diagnosis
rows.titleFr: Nettoyage partiel puis diagnostic

preconditions: The plugin is enabled; C3 uses liveprobe.fault.json with throwIn OnDisable.
scenario.operation: Make one cleanup step fail during disable or failed-enable cleanup, then retry.
scenario.expected: The failure is logged, the lifecycle never reports a cleanly disabled plugin while cleanup is incomplete, and a retry completes it.

rows.title: Plugin disabled between an allocation and its publication
rows.titleFr: désactivation entre allocation et publication

preconditions: A resource factory allocates a host resource; the plugin is disabled before the owner is published.
scenario.operation: Disable the plugin between the allocation and the publication of its owner.
scenario.expected: The operation is refused, or reported with an unknown effect, and exactly one compensation is reported.

rows.title: Two plugins sharing or not sharing the SDK assemblies
rows.titleFr: Deux plugins partageant ou non les assemblies SDK

preconditions: Coexistence plugins A and B built from the exact CI package.
scenario.operation: Load A and B in one Cheat Engine session, record the plugin and Hosting assembly identities, then disable A while B keeps working and re-enable A.
scenario.expected: Assembly MVIDs, load contexts and PluginHost static identity are measured; enable and removal of A and B are independent as the profile announces.

rows.title: Coexistence with one shared SDK assemblies folder
rows.titleFr: Deux plugins utilisant les mêmes bibliothèques

preconditions: A and B copied into one folder; the runner refuses a same-named file with different bytes.
scenario.operation: Run the Q09 sequence with both plugins loaded from the shared folder.
scenario.expected: The measured identities show whether A and B share one Hosting instance; each plugin keeps working while the other is removed.

rows.title: Coexistence with separate plugin folders
rows.titleFr: Deux plugins partageant ou non les assemblies SDK

preconditions: A and B in separate folders, each with its own SDK assemblies.
scenario.operation: Run the Q09 sequence with each plugin loaded from its own folder.
scenario.expected: The measured identities show which SDK assemblies each plugin uses; each plugin keeps working while the other is removed.

rows.title: Two package versions in separate folders
rows.titleFr: Deux versions de paquet dans répertoires séparés

preconditions: A plugin on one SDK package version and a plugin on another, each in its own folder.
scenario.operation: Load both in one Cheat Engine session and record the assemblies each one actually uses.
scenario.expected: The assemblies really used and the behaviour of both plugins are recorded.

rows.title: Missing Lua module or incomplete exports
rows.titleFr: Module Lua absent ou exports incomplets

preconditions: No lua53-64.dll in the process, or a module that lacks exports the SDK binds.
scenario.operation: Enable the plugin.
scenario.expected: The enable is refused before any plugin code and no second Lua runtime is loaded; when the host module is present it is found without loading another.

rows.title: Allocation failure while growing the Lua stack
rows.titleFr: Échec d’allocation pendant croissance de pile

preconditions: Native Lua fixture with an allocator that rejects the growth.
scenario.operation: Grow the stack or push a generated closure while the allocation fails.
scenario.expected: An error status is returned and the stack is restored.

rows.title: Failure of string, table, userdata or reference creation
rows.titleFr: Échec de string/table/userdata/ref

preconditions: Native Lua fixture with an allocator that fails at each creation point.
scenario.operation: Create a string, table, userdata or registry reference while the allocation fails.
scenario.expected: No Lua error crosses a managed frame; the failure is reported as a status.

rows.title: Managed callback that throws
rows.titleFr: Callback managé qui lève une exception

preconditions: A managed Lua callback is registered; C3 calls ce77_live_probe_throw_managed_exception under pcall.
scenario.operation: Throw a managed exception inside the callback thunk.
scenario.expected: The caller receives a catchable Lua error after the thunk returns, and the next call on the same state works.

rows.title: Callback kept after disable
rows.titleFr: Callback conservé après disable

preconditions: A script kept a reference to a plugin callback; C3 uses ce77_live_probe_prepare_callback_shutdown.
scenario.operation: Disable the plugin, then call the kept callback under pcall.
scenario.expected: The call is neutralized with an error and no managed state is freed behind a live closure.

rows.title: Global collision, replacement, then third-party replacement
rows.titleFr: Collision de global, remplacement puis remplacement tiers

preconditions: A Lua global of the same name already exists, or is replaced by a third party after registration.
scenario.operation: Register the global with the default and the replacing policy, then release the registration.
scenario.expected: A collision is refused by default, a replaced value is restored only while the registration still owns the global, and a third-party replacement is never overwritten.

rows.title: Controlled Lua state replacement
rows.titleFr: Remplacement contrôlé d’état Lua

preconditions: References and callbacks exist before the SDK-controlled state reset.
scenario.operation: Run the SDK state-reset transition, then use the old references and callbacks.
scenario.expected: Attach epoch and state generation stay coherent, old references are refused, and old callbacks are neutralized before the state is replaced.

rows.title: Use of a reference after an external reset
rows.titleFr: Tentative d’usage d’une ref après reset externe

preconditions: LiveProbe enabled; the operator calls resetLuaState() from the Lua Engine between the two snapshots.
scenario.operation: Capture a reference before an external reset the SDK was not told about, then try to use it.
scenario.expected: The outcome is recorded and reported as an unsupported profile; no safety is claimed that the run does not show.

rows.title: First calls from two workers
rows.titleFr: Premiers appels depuis deux workers

preconditions: Two worker threads, and at C4 two SDK copies, make their first Lua-bound calls.
scenario.operation: Start the first calls concurrently from the workers.
scenario.expected: Either the serialization policy is demonstrated or the calls are not admitted; the conservative default admits them only on the main thread.

rows.title: Bytes with NUL and multibyte strings
rows.titleFr: Bytes contenant NUL et chaînes multioctets

preconditions: Strings with embedded NUL bytes, multibyte UTF-8 and invalid sequences.
scenario.operation: Pass and read them through the SDK string and byte bindings.
scenario.expected: The exact binary length is kept and every text conversion is explicit.

rows.title: Signed and unsigned 32-bit values and 64-bit boundaries
rows.titleFr: 32 bits signés / non signés et 64 bits limites

preconditions: Values at the 32-bit and 64-bit signed and unsigned boundaries.
scenario.operation: Write and read them through the memory and integer bindings.
scenario.expected: No value passes through a double that loses bits.

rows.title: nil, false, zero, zero results and Lua error
rows.titleFr: nil, faux, zéro, zéro résultat et erreur Lua

preconditions: A binding whose Lua target can return each of these shapes.
scenario.operation: Call it for each shape.
scenario.expected: The results stay distinguishable as the member defines them.

rows.title: CE object, light userdata and foreign userdata
rows.titleFr: Objet CE, light userdata et userdata tiers

preconditions: A Cheat Engine object, a light userdata and a foreign full userdata such as an io.open handle.
scenario.operation: Pass each one where the SDK expects a Cheat Engine object.
scenario.expected: The trust domain is explicit: only the qualified provider path is accepted and incompatible forms are refused.

rows.title: Bound method and 0-based indexers
rows.titleFr: Méthode liée et indexeurs 0-based

preconditions: A Cheat Engine class with methods and 0-based indexers.
scenario.operation: Call a bound method and read indexed members.
scenario.expected: No self argument is added by mistake and the 0-based indices are kept.

rows.title: Scanner created, then list creation or publication fails
rows.titleFr: Création scanner puis échec de liste / publication

preconditions: A scanner is created and a later child creation or managed publication fails.
scenario.operation: Inject the failure after the scanner exists.
scenario.expected: Children are rolled back before the parent and a cleanup failure stays visible.

rows.title: FirstScan, NextScan, results and destruction
rows.titleFr: FirstScan / NextScan / résultats / destruction

preconditions: QualificationTarget running with an Int32/Int64 value cell that changes on the step command.
scenario.operation: Run a first scan, change the value, run a next scan, read the results and destroy the scan objects.
scenario.expected: The sequence is valid and every object has a single owner that destroys it once.

rows.title: AOB scan: empty, error and malformed result
rows.titleFr: AOB : vide, erreur, résultat mal formé

preconditions: A pattern absent from the target (zero matches), a failing call and a malformed result.
scenario.operation: Run the AOB scan for each case.
scenario.expected: Absence and error are never merged into one outcome; on this host zero matches arrive as no value, which the SDK reports as the factual NoResult category.

rows.title: AOB scan in a module with matches outside the module
rows.titleFr: AOB dans module avec résultats hors module

preconditions: QualificationTarget with a module-resident marker and heap copies of it.
scenario.operation: Scan for the marker restricted to the module.
scenario.expected: The filter is exact, and a native cost is never presented as bounded when the results are post-filtered.

rows.title: Result limit and cancellation during copy
rows.titleFr: Limite de résultats et annulation pendant copie

preconditions: QualificationTarget region with many repetitions of a pattern.
scenario.operation: Scan with a result limit, and cancel while the results are copied.
scenario.expected: Truncation and cancellation are explicit and the result list is released.

rows.title: Reused PID and target switch
rows.titleFr: Même PID réutilisé / changement de cible

preconditions: Owners created against target A; the operator switches the target.
scenario.operation: Switch between targets and reuse PIDs before releasing the owners.
scenario.expected: An old owner is refused or released through its qualified origin context, never redirected to another target.

rows.title: Targets A and B and a reused PID
rows.titleFr: cible A/B et PID réutilisé

preconditions: Two QualificationTarget instances; the receipt states how PID reuse was obtained and never claims one that did not happen.
scenario.operation: Switch A to B to A, or restart a target to reuse its PID, with owners still alive.
scenario.expected: Owners of the previous target are refused, never applied to the new process.

rows.title: Cleanup after a target switch
rows.titleFr: cleanup après changement de cible

preconditions: An allocation made in target A; the operator selects target B.
scenario.operation: Release the allocation after the switch.
scenario.expected: Cleanup never calls an ambient deallocation in B; it is refused and the residue is reported.

rows.title: File opened as a process
rows.titleFr: fichier comme processus

preconditions: A file opened as a process instead of a live target.
scenario.operation: Use the SDK process-bound operations on it.
scenario.expected: Refused at C1; NotApplicable at C3 because the lab qualifies local processes only.

C3.justification: The qualified backend of the profile is LocalProcess only; no file opened as a process is an authorized lab target. The C1 refusal is the evidence for this sub-row.

rows.title: CEServer target
rows.titleFr: CEServer

preconditions: A target reached through CEServer.
scenario.operation: Use the SDK process-bound operations on it.
scenario.expected: Refused at C1; NotApplicable at C3 because no CEServer exists in the lab.

C3.justification: No CEServer exists in the lab and the qualified backend is LocalProcess only. The C1 refusal is the evidence for this sub-row.

rows.title: Reuse of an old allocation address
rows.titleFr: réutilisation d’une ancienne adresse d’allocation

preconditions: An allocation was released and its address can be handed out again.
scenario.operation: Use an owner of the old allocation after its address was reused.
scenario.expected: The stale owner is refused and never releases the new allocation.

rows.title: Overridden Cheat Engine pointer size
rows.titleFr: Pointer size CE surchargée

preconditions: setPointerSize is called after the last target selection, because openProcess resets it; the value is verified right before the snapshot and restored after it.
scenario.operation: Observe the configured pointer size next to the process architecture on a 64-bit target.
scenario.expected: The configured size is reported as a fact distinct from the process width.

rows.title: Configured pointer size smaller than the process width
rows.titleFr: pointeur configuré plus petit que la largeur du processus

preconditions: getPointerSize() returns 4 on a 64-bit target.
scenario.operation: Use the pointer codecs while the configured size is smaller than the process width.
scenario.expected: The two observations stay distinct and pointer codecs are refused or flagged.

rows.title: x86, x64, ARM or unknown host and target backends
rows.titleFr: Hôte/cible x86, x64, ARM ou backend inconnu

preconditions: A target is selected; with no target selected the SDK reports that first.
scenario.operation: Observe the instruction set and width for each host and target combination.
scenario.expected: An unknown value is reported rather than an instruction set deduced from the 64-bit flag alone; on x64 both the x86-family and 64-bit flags are set.

rows.title: x64 target
rows.titleFr: Hôte/cible x86, x64, ARM ou backend inconnu

preconditions: QualificationTarget x64 selected on the x64 host.
scenario.operation: Observe the target profile and width.
scenario.expected: X64 is reported: x86 family and 64-bit.

rows.title: x86 target
rows.titleFr: Hôte/cible x86, x64, ARM ou backend inconnu

preconditions: QualificationTarget x86 or gtutorial-i386.exe selected on the x64 host.
scenario.operation: Observe the target profile and width.
scenario.expected: X86 is reported with a 4-byte pointer width.

rows.title: x86 Cheat Engine host
rows.titleFr: Hôte/cible x86, x64, ARM ou backend inconnu

preconditions: An x86 Cheat Engine executable.
scenario.operation: Load the SDK plugin into it.
scenario.expected: Unsupported: the SDK is x64-only, so the route is refused.

C3.justification: The SDK and its native bridge are x64-only; an x86 Cheat Engine host (cheatengine-i386.exe) cannot load them and is an unsupported route of the profile.

rows.title: ARM or unknown backend
rows.titleFr: Hôte/cible x86, x64, ARM ou backend inconnu

preconditions: Facts that describe an ARM target or no known architecture.
scenario.operation: Derive the target profile from them.
scenario.expected: Unknown is reported instead of a guessed instruction set.

C3.justification: No ARM host and no unknown backend exist in the lab; the C1 cell covers the unknown-value behaviour.

rows.title: Memory batch that fails after several writes
rows.titleFr: Lot mémoire avec échec après plusieurs écritures

preconditions: A Client memory batch whose later write fails.
scenario.operation: Run the batch.
scenario.expected: The number of completed writes and the partial effect are exposed.

C1.justification: Client-owned scenario: the SDK has no Client composition to test. It is qualified in the Client matrix, https://github.com/CheatEngineNet/CheatEngine.Client/blob/main/docs/qualification/matrix.json.

C3.justification: Client-owned scenario: the SDK has no Client composition to test. It is qualified in the Client matrix, https://github.com/CheatEngineNet/CheatEngine.Client/blob/main/docs/qualification/matrix.json.

rows.title: Record destroyed or table reloaded
rows.titleFr: Record détruit ou table rechargée

preconditions: A memory record owner exists; the record is destroyed or the table reloaded.
scenario.operation: Use the old reference after the destruction or reload.
scenario.expected: The old reference is never reused as a new record.

rows.title: Script activation, then incomplete rollback
rows.titleFr: Activation de script puis rollback incomplet

preconditions: An auto-assembler script is activated and its rollback fails part-way.
scenario.operation: Activate the script, then deactivate it with a failing step.
scenario.expected: The disable token and the unconfirmed effects are kept and reported.

rows.title: One-shot timer finished before Dispose
rows.titleFr: Timer one-shot terminé avant Dispose

preconditions: A one-shot timer created with createTimer(delay, function) has already fired.
scenario.operation: Dispose its token after it fired.
scenario.expected: The timer object is never destroyed a second time.

rows.title: Hotkey callback during module shutdown
rows.titleFr: Callback hotkey pendant arrêt de module

preconditions: A hotkey keeps firing while the plugin disables.
scenario.operation: Trigger the hotkey during disable.
scenario.expected: The callback is either still rooted or neutralized; it never runs against freed state.

rows.title: Debug or process-watcher event on a secondary thread
rows.titleFr: Événement debug / process watcher sur thread secondaire

preconditions: A native plugin route that registers a debug-event or process-watcher callback.
scenario.operation: Deliver the event on a secondary thread.
scenario.expected: The signature and thread affinity are measured and the GUI is never touched illegally.

C3.justification: Profile decision CPA-2: the managed-hostfxr route has no classic native registration, so a debug or process-watcher event never reaches an SDK plugin on this profile (the classic dispatcher is internal). Reopen if a native route is decided; the C1 dispatcher tests stay with their owner.

rows.title: Reduced or mutated classic exports table
rows.titleFr: Réduction / mutation de table d’exports classique

preconditions: A classic exports table whose declared size is smaller than the SDK prefix or whose buffer is truncated.
scenario.operation: Copy the table prefix the SDK reads.
scenario.expected: No slot beyond the declared size and no nil slot is called; a reduced or truncated table is refused.

C3.justification: Profile decision CPA-2: a managed-hostfxr plugin receives the managed exports record, never the classic exports table, whose route stays documentary in 2.0. The C1 refusal tests cover the SDK reader.

rows.title: Clean installation from the package
rows.titleFr: Installation propre depuis paquet

preconditions: A plugin folder built from the exact CI package with an isolated NuGet package folder, outside any workspace.
scenario.operation: Load the plugin from that folder and record where every SDK assembly and the bridge were loaded from.
scenario.expected: Nothing is taken implicitly from a development workspace; the bridge equals the packaged one.

rows.title: NativeAOT publish and export inspection
rows.titleFr: Publication AOT et inspection des exports

preconditions: A NativeAOT library publish of an SDK consumer.
scenario.operation: Publish it and inspect the exports of the native image.
scenario.expected: The expected export surface is present and no Cheat Engine load promise is added.

rows.title: Removal of a NativeAOT plugin profile
rows.titleFr: Retrait d’un éventuel profil plugin NativeAOT

preconditions: A NativeAOT plugin loaded by Cheat Engine.
scenario.operation: Unload it through the host plugin removal.
scenario.expected: The residence model complies with the runtime limitations and is validated before any support is announced.

C3.justification: Profile decision CPA-2 and F02: the NativeAOT plugin route is unsupported; .NET does not support unloading a NativeAOT library with FreeLibrary (https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/native-aot/libraries).

C4.justification: Profile decision CPA-2 and F02: the NativeAOT plugin route is unsupported, so there is no second NativeAOT plugin to remove next to another one.

rows.title: Client cleanup with a faulty module
rows.titleFr: Nettoyage Client avec module fautif

preconditions: A Client host with several modules, one of which fails during cleanup.
scenario.operation: Stop the Client host.
scenario.expected: Every later cleanup is still attempted and the errors are aggregated.

C1.justification: Client-owned scenario: the SDK has no Client composition to test. It is qualified in the Client matrix, https://github.com/CheatEngineNet/CheatEngine.Client/blob/main/docs/qualification/matrix.json.

C3.justification: Client-owned scenario: the SDK has no Client composition to test. It is qualified in the Client matrix, https://github.com/CheatEngineNet/CheatEngine.Client/blob/main/docs/qualification/matrix.json.

rows.title: A contract-only API is called
rows.titleFr: Une API contract-only est appelée

preconditions: A Client API that is declared but not implemented on this package.
scenario.operation: Call it.
scenario.expected: An explicit unavailable result is returned, never a false success.

C1.justification: Client-owned scenario: the SDK has no Client composition to test. It is qualified in the Client matrix, https://github.com/CheatEngineNet/CheatEngine.Client/blob/main/docs/qualification/matrix.json.

C3.justification: Client-owned scenario: the SDK has no Client composition to test. It is qualified in the Client matrix, https://github.com/CheatEngineNet/CheatEngine.Client/blob/main/docs/qualification/matrix.json.

rows.title: Sensitive availability probe
rows.titleFr: Probe de disponibilité sensible

preconditions: A Client capability probe for an optional family.
scenario.operation: Probe the capability.
scenario.expected: No driver is loaded, nothing is executed remotely and the target is not changed.

C1.justification: Client-owned scenario: the SDK has no Client composition to test. It is qualified in the Client matrix, https://github.com/CheatEngineNet/CheatEngine.Client/blob/main/docs/qualification/matrix.json.

C3.justification: Client-owned scenario: the SDK has no Client composition to test. It is qualified in the Client matrix, https://github.com/CheatEngineNet/CheatEngine.Client/blob/main/docs/qualification/matrix.json.

rows.title: Logs containing user data or expressions
rows.titleFr: Logs contenant données utilisateur ou expressions

preconditions: Operations whose arguments contain user data or Lua expressions.
scenario.operation: Log them at every level.
scenario.expected: Sensitive fields are excluded unless explicitly opted in.

rows.title: Inherited property or method and public alias
rows.titleFr: Propriété/méthode héritée ou alias public

preconditions: A Cheat Engine class that inherits a member or exposes it through an alias.
scenario.operation: Resolve and call the member through the SDK projection.
scenario.expected: The resolution matches the host and the provenance of the alias is kept.

rows.title: SDK package updated without adapting the Client
rows.titleFr: Paquet SDK mis à jour sans adaptation Client

preconditions: A newer SDK package than the one the Client was built against.
scenario.operation: Build the Client consumer contracts against it.
scenario.expected: The gap is detected by the consumer contract tests before publication, not discovered after it.

C0.justification: SDK-side static contract only: the ApiCompat baseline suppressions, the removed PublicAPI lines and the reviewed invisible changes against CheatEngine.SDK 1.0.0 agree, and breaks on Client-consumed types are listed. It never closes Q48 at C1 or C3 (Client consumer contracts, advisory client-canary) and never closes F05.
